title: Attention Is All You Need
abstract: Introduces the Transformer, a sequence model built entirely from self-attention and feed-forward layers, removing recurrence and convolution. Uses multi-head attention, positional encodings, and residual connections. Trains faster than recurrent alternatives because attention parallelises across sequence positions.

title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
abstract: Formulates generation as learning to reverse a gradual noising process. Trains a network to predict the noise added at each timestep, then samples by iteratively denoising from Gaussian noise. Establishes diffusion as competitive with adversarial approaches for image synthesis.

title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models
abstract: Moves the diffusion process from pixel space into the latent space of a pretrained autoencoder, cutting compute substantially while preserving quality. Adds cross-attention conditioning so the same backbone handles text-to-image, inpainting, and super-resolution.

title: Video Diffusion Models
abstract: Extends image diffusion to video by replacing the 2D U-Net with a 3D variant factorised over space and time. Introduces gradient-based conditioning for generating longer sequences than the training horizon. Reports the temporal coherence problem as the dominant failure mode.

title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
abstract: Trains image and text encoders jointly with a contrastive objective over a large corpus of image-caption pairs. The resulting joint embedding supports zero-shot classification by comparing an image against text descriptions of candidate labels.

title: ViViT: A Video Vision Transformer
abstract: Applies transformers to video by extracting spatio-temporal tokens from the input clip. Compares several factorisations of spatial and temporal attention, finding that factorised encoders trade accuracy for a large reduction in compute on long clips.

title: Flamingo: a Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning
abstract: Bridges frozen vision encoders and frozen language models with gated cross-attention layers and a perceiver resampler. Accepts interleaved sequences of images, video, and text, enabling few-shot adaptation to vision-language tasks without task-specific finetuning.

title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
abstract: Freezes pretrained weights and injects trainable low-rank decomposition matrices into each layer, reducing trainable parameters by orders of magnitude. Adds no inference latency because the update can be merged back into the base weights.

title: Training Language Models to Follow Instructions with Human Feedback
abstract: Collects human preference comparisons, fits a reward model to them, then optimises the policy against that reward with reinforcement learning under a KL penalty to the supervised baseline. Reports that smaller aligned models are preferred over much larger unaligned ones.

title: Direct Preference Optimization
abstract: Shows that the RLHF objective admits a closed-form solution allowing preference learning without training a separate reward model or running online reinforcement learning. Optimises a classification loss directly on preference pairs.

title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
abstract: Interleaves chain-of-thought reasoning traces with environment actions, letting the model plan, gather external evidence, and revise. Reduces hallucination relative to reasoning-only prompting on knowledge-intensive tasks.

title: Make-A-Video: Text-to-Video Generation without Text-Video Data
abstract: Learns text-to-video by transferring a text-to-image prior and learning motion from unlabelled video, avoiding the need for paired text-video corpora. Uses spatiotemporal super-resolution to raise frame rate and resolution.

title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
abstract: Finds power-law relationships between model loss and compute, dataset size, and parameter count. Argues that for a fixed compute budget, larger models trained on less data outperform smaller models trained to convergence.

title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
abstract: Shows that prompting a model to produce intermediate reasoning steps substantially improves arithmetic and symbolic reasoning, and that the effect emerges only above a certain model scale.
